Self Storage Income · Readiness Score · design directions v1

Three ways to make the quiz worth taking

Three skins over one interaction model, ordered light to dark so the choice reads as a single spectrum rather than three unrelated ideas. Every phone below is a real, clickable 375px flow: pick an answer and it advances, exactly as the built page would.

The question content is not retyped for this page. It is read from the locked v2.1 set in build-readiness-v2-doc.js and hashed, so the page can prove at runtime that nothing drifted.

"Put the contact info collection at the END of the form not at the beginning."  /  "Make this sexy like a landing page. I want to WANT to take this thing, not have to. I love the simplicity, no need to change that, but I want sexy juicy page vibes."Gray, 22 Sept 2026

DIRECTION 1

Framed Card

Light page. The card wears a navy header band as app chrome, so blue is present as a band rather than as a field.

Safest of the three to read across 13 screens. Reads as a well-made tool.

DIRECTION 2

Blue Stage

Full-bleed SSI navy carrying the warm page grid and glow. The white card floats on a deep shadow with the logo knocked out above it.

Gero's suggestion. Highest continuity with the shipped /ind-overpay page.

DIRECTION 3

Deep Navy

The card itself is dark. Glass option tiles, a cyan selection glow, white type on #082743.

The most juicy and the most risk: long-form reading and the video embed both fight a dark surface.

True of all three, so it does not need re-deciding per column

  • Contact moved to the end. It now sits after the free-text note, prefilled from the link parameters the app already accepts, and framed as a confirm rather than a form.
  • Progress stops at the note. The rail fills to 100% there and the contact step sits past it, outside the counted flow. Calling it "step 14 of 14" would undo the point of the reframe.
  • The intro copy sells the taker. The live page says answers go to the person you are speaking with, which is a benefit for SSI. That is the real reason nobody wants to take it, and skin alone does not fix it.
  • One question per screen, untouched. Gray asked us to protect the simplicity, so the interaction model is identical across all three.
  • Motion. CTA lift plus a shine sweep and a press state, a tick that pops on select, a step that slides in. All of it behind prefers-reduced-motion, which the self-check enforces by selector.
  • Contrast. The orange CTA keeps its near-black label throughout. White on #f39610 is 2.3:1 and fails; the self-check prints every pair.

Open, and deliberately not fixed here

  • Submissions on the live page currently go nowhere. The shipped bundle reads VITE_READINESS_WEBHOOK_URL and that key is absent from the inlined env object, so the submit request short-circuits and returns false. Every completed assessment is being discarded. One key on the ssirdscfr Vercel project. Worth shipping on its own so there is a completion baseline to compare the redesign against.
  • "Internal use only / Start form" and "Internal preview only / Start over" render on the live prospect-facing page. Not drawn in any of these mockups. Removing them from the live page is still an open call.
  • Copy is a working draft, not Natalya's. Headline, the three intro lines and the contact-step wording all need her pass.
  • For Gray: is this quiz ever linked cold or organic, or only ever sent as a setter link? Contact-at-the-end takes abandonment capture to zero, which is fine precisely because identity comes from contact_id in the URL. If it is ever linked cold, a cold abandoner becomes unrecoverable.
  • Name, call time and the prefilled contact values are placeholders. The email uses the reserved example.com domain so nothing here can be mistaken for a real prospect.
